newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnians protest about Dayton's "broken" promises.
newsitem.headline: Bosnians protest about Dayton's "broken" promises.

text.p: Several thousand people protested on Tuesday in central Sarajevo against what they said was the international community's failure to honour promises made in the Dayton peace accord, which ended 43 months of war.

The protesters, who gathered at the city's memorial to World War Two partisan soldiers, said that pledges to arrest indicted war criminals, guarantee freedom of movement and enable refugees to return home had not been fulfilled.

Most of the protesters were women from the once U.N.- protected Moslem enclave of Srebrenica, which was overrun by Bosnian Serbs in the summer of 1995. About 8,000 people, mainly men and boys, from the area disappeared and are presumed dead.

"I'm from Srebrenica and I'm fed up being humiliated," said one 18-year-old girl. "I lost my father and my two brothers and nobody knows where they are. I want to talk to somebody who can give me answers."

The crowd made its way to the office of international mediator Carl Bildt, where his deputy, German diplomat Michael Steiner was jostled by the angry women as he left the buildling. They pummelled his car with their fists as he drove off.

The crowd blocked traffic at one of the city's main road junctions. Western diplomatic sources said the protest may have been aimed at drawing attention to Moslem concerns ahead of next week's London conference on the Dayton peace process.
